citeAs: The EgoLife Team (2025). EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv.
description: EgoLife is a comprehensive ultra-long egocentric daily life dataset collected from six participants living together for one week, with multimodal egocentric video from Meta Aria glasses, synchronized third-person video, and multimodal signals such as mmWave radar. The dataset contains about 300 hours of egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life data with intensive annotations including transcripts, captions, and QA benchmarks.
name: EgoLife
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper states that the 50-hour transcript was reviewed for accuracy, narrations and captions were reviewed and corrected by human annotators, visual-audio captions were verified by human annotators, and QA candidates were filtered from around 100K candidates to 1K high-quality questions per participant and finally curated to 500 QA per participant through rigorous selection and refinement.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotations were created by merging audio from six participants, applying speech recognition to generate timestamped transcripts, using diarization to separate speakers, then manually reviewing and refining each participant’s audible speech. Caption annotations were produced by splitting videos into 5-minute clips slowed to 0.8× speed, having annotators continuously narrate actions, interactions, and environment details, transcribing and correcting those narrations, then merging and expanding them into visual-audio captions with GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini and human verification. QA annotations were generated by prompting GPT-4o on visual-audio captions to create timestamped candidate questions, which annotators filtered, refined, added distractors to, and annotated for audio requirement and look-back time.
rai:dataBiases: The project intentionally started with a narrow setting, sacrificing some generalizability such as a single language and scenario. The paper also notes plans to expand to broader languages, locations, and activities, acknowledging current coverage limitations.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected over a seven-day period with six volunteers residing together in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses to capture multimodal egocentric videos, while 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras and two mmWave devices provided synchronized third-person and multimodal reference data; an additional one-day Milan session was also collected later.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Due to storage limitations, recordings were collected in three-hour segments with approximately one hour needed for data upload and storage clearance; during this period participants were instructed to remain in their rooms and limit activities to avoid disruptions in the recorded footage.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes first-person video from 6 Aria glasses, third-person video from fixed indoor cameras, synchronized multimodal signal data including millimeter-wave radars and WiFi signals, plus audio, IMU, and gaze streams from the Aria devices.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: seven days for the Beijing session; one day for the Milan session
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Experiments
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently reflects a narrow setting with limited generalizability, especially single-language and single-scenario coverage in the main Beijing release. The authors state plans to expand to more languages, locations, and activities, indicating current limitations in coverage and diversity.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Recordings were structured into three-hour segments because of storage limitations. For captioning, videos were split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8× speed. Initial narration phrases were merged into coherent captions, and representative frames were sampled at 1 FPS and paired with transcripts to create expanded visual-audio captions. Only QA questions requiring information from at least five minutes prior were retained.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data underwent synchronization across video, audio, IMU, GoPro, and other signals; signal extraction and alignment; de-identification via face, license plate, screen-content blurring; muting of sensitive audio; splitting videos into clips; transcript generation with speech recognition and diarization; and conversion of narrations into merged and visual-audio captions.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is described as an ongoing project, with the Milan dataset to be detailed in an upcoming EgoLife blog series, a continuing annotation partnership for future EgoLife versions, and plans to expand the dataset to broader languages, locations, and activities.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that EgoLife and EgoButler could enhance personalized assistance, contextual reminders, learning, task tracking, and support for elderly people or people with cognitive challenges, while emphasizing the need to address privacy, user autonomy, trust, data privacy safeguards, and transparency in AI decision-making.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for research on egocentric AI assistants, long-context life-oriented question answering, human behavior recognition, multimodal signal analysis, human-machine interaction, long-duration activity understanding, interpersonal dynamics, contextual interactions, and personalized assistance tasks such as locating items, recalling events, tracking habits, analyzing social interactions, and making recommendations.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Speech recognition using Whisper Large v3, an open-source diarization algorithm, GPT-4o-mini for merging narration phrases, GPT-4o for summarizing captions and generating QA candidates, a transcription tool for converting spoken narrations to text, and GPT-based tools for initial QA generation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The raw recordings may contain participant faces, bystanders’ faces, vehicle license plates, sensitive screen content such as passwords or personal data, spoken private or potentially identifiable information in audio, and participant identity information; the released data is de-identified through blurring and audio muting.
